answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions through a stake-backed reputation registry: each identity locks funds, and counterparties accept work only after checking its history of completed, non-reversed tasks. If a fake agent cheats, a dispute burns its stake and removes its record; creating replacements does not restore that history. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock fresh capital for every identity and keep it at risk through a long horizon, while a vine of linked accounts can still be exposed if they reuse payment routes. A gale of cheap accounts alone earns no trust.
